The hack exposed everything. Emails. Passwords. Financial records. Forty million accounts compromised in a single breach. The company knew about the vulnerability for months. Internal memos show engineers flagged the problem twice. Management ignored them both times. The cost of a fix was estimated at two million dollars. The cost of the breach -- lawsuits, settlements, lost customers -- will exceed one billion. This is the math that keeps security experts up at night. Prevention is cheap. Recovery is not. Congress held hearings. Executives testified. They expressed regret. They promised reforms. The stock price dipped for a week and then recovered. Nobody went to jail. The affected customers got two years of free credit monitoring -- a gesture so hollow it borders on insult. Until there are real consequences for negligence, breaches like this will keep happening. That is not a prediction. It is a certainty.
